question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
trigger: The user challenged whether parseAuthoredHtmlDocument, parseHtmlDocument, parseHtmlSlice, serializeHtml, and importDocx used the cleanest standard vocabulary, and asked whether conversion should use codec encode/decode names, editor APIs, or pure functions.
requirements: Choose names from the operation law rather than force symmetry across text syntax, package files, persistence codecs, and installed editor conveniences.
Make the default HTML and Markdown parse mean one complete document; suffix only slice and inline variants.
Keep standalone HTML and Markdown functions for detached and server work and editor namespace methods for already compiled installed configuration, both over one private implementation.
Reserve encode/decode and codec for paired typed representations with explicit direction laws.
Keep DOCX as an asynchronous import/export package workflow with comments, retained source, assets, limits, cancellation, and native review behavior.
Delete hidden authored documents from HTML and Markdown unless a distinct current caller proves that transport job.
Keep canonical authored JSON as the exact Plate review format and DOCX revisions plus its authored package part as the Word review format.
Retain the compiled plugin schema, diagnosed format recovery, loss-policy, document/slice carriers, and DataTransfer ownership from the prior schema-admission review.
Break old names without compatibility aliases on next.
evidenceReuse: Reused the fixed 405-row conversion ontology, typed-codec and editor-candidate shards, schema-admission review, and export architecture only where their requirements still held. Re-read the current HTML, Markdown, static HTML, authored JSON, DOCX, import/export toolbar, docs, and type-test paths; swept production callers for review-envelope use; and compared the naming laws already source-bound for Zod and Effect codecs, Circe, Serde, parse5, unified, ProseMirror, Tiptap, Lexical, CKEditor, and Pandoc. Two bounded independent hard-cut audits agreed on parse/serialize vocabulary and pure/editor ownership; the stricter audit found no production HTML/Markdown authored-envelope caller and defeated the proposed trusted-restore API.
summary: Pursue the conversion plan with a smaller public surface. Use parseHtml/parseHtmlSlice/serializeHtml and parseMarkdown/parseMarkdownSlice/parseMarkdownInline/serializeMarkdown; installed editor namespaces expose parse, parseSlice, parseInline, and serialize over the same private runtime. Document is redundant on the default parse. Reserve encode/decode for typed codec pairs. Keep importDocx/exportDocx as standalone package workflows and cut the redundant To. Delete HTML and Markdown authored envelopes, review projections, trust options, and authored parsers: exact review state already belongs to canonical authored JSON, while Word review belongs to DOCX revisions and its format-owned authored part. Retain the prior schema-admission, diagnostics, recovery, and document/slice laws.

reconciliation.question: Which schema should validate canonical editor documents, when may import recover, what must export reject, and does Plite need another validation layer?
reconciliation.reason: The compiled plugin schema, diagnosed recovery, default rejection of lossy repair, strict export/persistence admission, and diagnosed DataTransfer attempt laws remain unchanged.

reconciliation.question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
reconciliation.reason: Retains direct format ownership and the hard cut of a universal converter, but replaces verbose complete-document parse names and removes the unproven HTML/Markdown native-envelope lane.

reconciliation.question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
reconciliation.reason: The schema and recovery design remains valid, but its public vocabulary, authored HTML/Markdown entrypoints, trust types, digest dependency, and review projections are replaced by the smaller target recorded here.

alternatives: Use encode/decode for HTML, Markdown, and DOCX: Stop; these operations do not share one typed reversible codec law, and document/slice parsing plus lossy diagnostics break the pair.
Use import/export for every format: Stop; it hides the established parse/serialize syntax model and makes insertion slices awkward.
Keep parseHtmlDocument and parseMarkdownDocument: Stop; complete-document parsing is the default job, while Slice and Inline are the meaningful exceptions.
Expose only pure functions: Stop; installed editor callers would repeatedly restate or compile configuration already owned by the editor.
Expose only editor methods: Stop; detached, server, worker, migration, and test callers would construct fake editing runtimes.
Keep separate parseAuthoredHtmlDocument and parseAuthoredMarkdownDocument methods with explicit trust: Stop; they harden a duplicated persistence channel with no production caller.
Merge authoredTrust into ordinary HTML/Markdown parse: Stop; one syntax would still have two competing authorities and a dangerous option would become easier to invoke.
Delete HTML/Markdown authored envelopes and use authored JSON plus DOCX review: Pursue; each surviving format has one authority and a proven user job.
Move DOCX under editor.api.docx: Stop; one-shot async package conversion has no installed plugin lifecycle and already needs explicit file/source options.
Rename exportToDocx to exportDocx: Pursue; export already supplies direction and To adds no semantic information.
proofLimits: Design and source audit only. No product API, package export, implementation, caller, docs, test, browser route, DOCX artifact, or native viewer was changed or certified. Current HTML and Markdown code still emits and automatically restores hidden authored envelopes, still accepts review projection, and current DOCX export is still named exportToDocx until the amended plan is executed. External comparisons retain the fixed-source limits recorded in the research shards; one independent worker was unavailable and contributed no evidence.
